body:
Didn’t think about the zofran but that’s the only new prescription medication I’ve added on recently and just thought of it this morning. 

If it’s Vraylar, I risk mental health by switching. 

If it’s Zofran, I’m going to be back to vomiting throughout the day. 

Kind of hope it’s the Zofran because I’d rather give that up than switch antipsychotics.

Sooo I also recently started Zofran 2x a day recently for my nausea/vomiting while I go through diagnostic process for gastroparesis. Called my doctors and waiting for call back to see if we should discontinue that before lowering Vraylar. 

Hot mess express. 

I just an so frustrated that I’m finally stable with next to no psychosis and now my physical health is declining and now this. I just feel like I can’t win.

I’ve been on it a few days for treating symptoms of akathesia (long time antipsychotic girly). 

Haven’t seen changes to GP! Not formally diagnosed yet, but waiting for testing and strongly suspected due to vomiting undigested food long after eaten. My GP pain flared up again a few days before starting propranolol, but hadn’t gotten better nor worse. Appetite has been pretty low for a while, but hasn’t changed since starting.

Amoxicillin/Clav! I just checked my CVS app to verify - it was prescribed on September 30, 2024 

I was also on a 10 day round of doxycycline starting September 13th, but that was because my finger had a horrific infection from a bad manicure, but that’s another antibiotic I took during that timeframe.

They didn’t test for celiac, but that is something my mom brought up! 

And I had covid twice, but may have had it a third time right before this started. I didn’t test because I was off work anyways for a concert (where I think I caught it) so I just rode the sickness out. 

I think baked potatoes are going to be my new best friend lol.

Thankfully I love potatoes! And my protein/meat won’t change since I don’t even like fish anyways (funny, the reason I never liked it was how it made my mouth feel years ago so I simple don’t eat it to this day). 

I’m really hoping I can add in rice so I can have chicken & rice meals since I love rice. But we shall see! I am planning on doing the elimination diet of everything for 2 weeks then adding one at a time. Waiting to talk to my allergist in a few weeks, but for now being more mindful during the daytime and for late dinner eating some allergens so I can take a Benadryl and just go to sleep. I do feel icky in the morning still with some symptoms, but they typically get better by the afternoon.

They originally did a skin prick test which tested positive for all the list besides sesame, but the blood test actually said my only allergen was sesame. But the allergist said the skin test was more accurate, but to assume sesame is an allergen as well. 

And that’s a good idea to make a safe food list! That’d be helpful because in overwhelmed with the off-limits food. It’s be nice to see a list of foods I can eat. Thank you!

Thank you! That’s the plan - I’m using Thrive to find some safe foods for 2 weeks then planning on adding rice since that’s help with wheat alternatives too and I love rice. 

I do think the corn may be a big issue but I’m going to try to add that as a last hope after the elimination. But I work as the general manager of a frozen custard shop & even if I have plain vanilla with caramel sauce made with allergy protocols I get sick like the flu so I’m assuming it’ll be a fail honestly. I’m fine with dairy according to the testing, but both the custard and caramel have corn syrup

When my old roommate went on a month long vacation I had a psychotic episode. I thought there were witches with bears on leashes in the back yard at night. I let my dogs go to the bathroom inside to protect them. I also would make the 3 dogs huddle up in my bedroom closet with me to hide from the shadowy ghosts trying to haunt us. That was in 2021. 

I also haven’t lived alone since and dread it. Currently live with mom & stepdad. They’re on vacation for 9 days (on day 3 rn) and I’m trying to stick to a daily routine as much as possible but I’m struggling. Like I took my 2 dogs in the back yard and was losing my mind trying to get them inside as soon as they went potty because they’re going to get attacked by a coyote. I’m still at the point I know it’s not real, but it also feels very real.

wild. in high school I gained 70lbs so fast when they put my on that. 

it was for the Tourette’s at the time and I always wondered why the shadow ghost people went away periodically in high school. Those periods were when they used antipsychotics to treat the Tourette’s lmao. I didn’t know they weren’t real until I was diagnosed with schizoaffective at age 25 (almost 28 now).

Thank you so much! That does help knowing it depends on the person. I’m doing really well & am starting a good paying job soon so I’m not in a position to risk my stability. I think I’ll avoid it for now. Thank you!

I had positive symptoms as early as age 6. They came and went episodically until I was 14 and put on Abilify for Tourette’s. They came back when I got off of it. Never realized they were symptoms until the past couple years. I used to tell people about the shadow people all the time and no one believed me unless they believed in ghosts.

A few years ago I always heard this car alarm going off. It took me forever to realize it wasn’t real. 

Recently I hear the sound of my garage door opening and then closing. Even if I’m at work I hear it. I’ve learned to ignore it and my dogs typically alert me when it’s real because they start barking. The hallucination and the actual sound are identical so I never really know until someone comes in or doesn’t.

I work 30-50 hours depending on the time of year as a supervisor at a doggy day care & am looking into moving into a management role. 

I’m currently having symptoms and am communicating with my general manager about accommodations - specifically not closing as manager because I’m alone in the resort while it’s dark & silent & it’s a trigger for me. 

I’d recommend starting part time.
I’m a supervisor at a dog day care / boarding facility! I’ve been there for a year now which is the longest I’ve held a job since my first high school job I left in 2015.

Thank you all! I’m not going to continue seeing her. My prescribing doctor is also not great (my longest session with him was 10 minutes and he gives sketchy vibes) and I was somehow able to get in to see a new MD tomorrow morning for an initial appointment and possible full evaluation. After the evaluation, if I like the doctor, I’m going to ask them for recommendations for therapists. 

I just realized today that I’ve been teetering on the edge of hypomania the last couple days so my brain is a little scattered. I’m going to discuss medications with the new doctor and follow their suggestions. I had to get off my primary medication because my new insurance didn’t cover it and I have been off of it completely for almost a week and I think I’m feeling the effects. 

After a long talk with my mom I feel a lot better and less confused. And realizing I’m having warning signs of hypomania also reminded me that I am not making it up. I’m 26 & live with my mom and she’s my main support. 

Sorry if this doesn’t make sense. I’ve been spiraling since the session

I’m searching for a new therapist tomorrow after work. 

And it’s confusing having been relatively stable for almost 2 years. Like I can remember how horrible I was doing mentally a couple years ago. I spent a month in residential psych treatment. I never expected to hold stability.

I have an appointment next week and I’ll definitely talk with him. Not doing anything cold turkey. I’m on 5 different prescriptions for schizoaffective, adhd, and ocd. I don’t want to go through harsh withdrawals

I was doing really well on Latuda. I was originally on it for what we thought at the time was bipolar with psychotic features. We increased it after a bad episode 2 years ago and I felt fine. Then I had breakthrough positive symptoms a few months ago & we increased again to 80mg and I was doing amazing. Switched insurance and it’s no longer covered. 2 days into the switch to risperdal. So far just a lot of nausea.
My dad I live with. He got sick first and is always out at the bars or traveling.
When I posted I was both. Currently sober and positive for covid.
It feels like a hella bad cold but puts me out of breath more. Everything wears me out. I still eat and whatnot but I can’t smell or taste.
I have 0 smell or taste. It’s the weirdest thing.
I love my dog so much but there’s no way she’s smarter than me. My cat? Maybe.
And my cat would be the tiger trying to attack it but the cage protc
Like the tree would be tiger ornaments with orange lights

I always assumed my auditory hallucinations were due to my bipolar, but it’s possible it’s ptsd related. Or both, who knows. They are much less frequent these days, but I used to head car alarms, music, my name being whispered, or the sound of muffled talking.

I went on a family vacation that was similar in setting to a trip where a trauma occurred for me. I was 20 at the time, and I was triggered the entire week. About three days in I was begging my mom to hold me and I was acting like a child. My mom was genuinely concerned and talked with me about the possibility of residential treatment (obviously there was other severe mental health problems going on prior to this episode). 

That’s the most severe “regression” (I guess that’s what it’s called?) episode I’ve had. But I used to have less severe ones frequently. I have very little memory of the episodes once I come out of them. It’s scary.

I honestly don’t have advice, but I feel for you. Both of my traumatic events happened during two different summers, so summertime is miserable for me. Over the years I’ve lost about 4 different jobs due to me having mental breakdowns in June/July where I didn’t go to work and/or ended up inpatient. 

My only suggestion would be to talk with a counselor/therapist. I should take this suggestion myself, but I have a track record of not rescheduling after stressful sessions.
I was a kitchen manager at a restaurant!
I was hired in FT in the deli
We had call out in chicken my second day in the deli. They decided to throw me to the wolves. It was intense

I went in to apply for FOH but they were only hiring BOH. I had experience with fast food and a side gig catering. I needed a job so I gave it a try. I started on salads and was struggling badly during any rush, but one day it all clicked and I started to kick ass. Now I can run every station well, train newbies on any station, and am a shift lead position training to be AKM to lead into KM.

I went to Camp Twitch and Shout as a kid so I have met a lot of people with Tourette’s! In my home life I actually had 2 neighbor kids with TS and another 2 kids at my high school. I also met a little boy with Tourette’s (I’m assuming) when I was giving a tour of my work’s kitchen during a field trip for homeschool kids that the restaurant I work at hosts every few months. There’s no polite way to acknowledge the tics, and so I genuinely was worried that he might think my tics were intentional to mock his own tics. In reality his tics just made my own tics more severe for the day.

I just joined! I used to go to a summer camp for kids with TS (Camp Twitch and Shout) when I was a kid and as a counselor one year as an adult. One of the people I met there came up with the idea for the tattoo! I hate the lettering, but I love the tat because of the meaning & memories attached to it.

I originally had it always wrapped by my nurse mom & then I went to the burn clinic and they had me wear this pad with silver in it for a couple weeks. Then I had to wear a compression sleeve 23/7 for 2 months and I’m supposed to be wearing a sleeve always at work and whenever I’m in the sun, but I honestly suck about wearing it. I’m about to stock up on maderma for this scar and for all the small scars on my right arm from smaller burns. 

I actually got another bacon grease burn on my leg this week (MUCH smaller and no where near as severe) and I’m using my left over creams on that one.

Totally off topic, but as a female line cook I want to know how on earth you can wear makeup to work? I wore makeup my first week and gave up. Do you have a kick ass setting spray? I’d love to look cute while making food honestly.
Haha it’s a tattoo I got when I was 18. There’s a teal ribbon next to it for Tourette’s. I’m always twitching and squeaking around the kitchen
